pairs.locus: Quintilian, Institutio Oratoria 7.3 (quoting Cicero, Pro Caecina)
pairs.question: Quid igitur fugiebant?
pairs.derivation: Cicero's chain of self-posed rhetorical questions quoted by Quintilian: "Quid igitur fugiebant? Propter metum. Quid metuebant? Vim videlicet..." First interrogative answered immediately by its own clause. Answer ends at the full stop before the next question "Quid metuebant". Self-contained: "Why then were they fleeing? Out of fear."

pairs.locus: Quintilian, Institutio Oratoria 7.3 (quoting Cicero, Pro Caecina)
pairs.question: Quid metuebant?
pairs.derivation: Second link of the same Ciceronian Q&A chain. Interrogative "Quid metuebant?" answered by "Vim videlicet."; answer cut at the full stop before "Potestis igitur principia negare..." (which turns from answering to a new argument). Self-contained: "What did they fear? Force, of course."

pairs.question: Quid est enim vulgo?
pairs.derivation: Quintilian quotes Cicero's definitional question-and-answer ("ut facit Cicero: 'Quid est enim vulgo? Vniversos'") as an example of varied finitio. The framing "ut facit Cicero" is dropped as narration. Genuine interrogative answered by a single word. Source orthography Vniversos preserved.
